name: Atlantic Equatorial Undercurrent
scope: Declared Atlantic equatorial subsurface-jet reach from the 35 W observational section to an OSW 5 E pre-island approach gate. Excludes western North Brazil retroflection source paths, island bifurcation near 6 E, downstream branches and westward returns. Not full source-to-termination length or an observed material trajectory.
layer: Subsurface equatorial/thermocline jet. At 35 W the reported mean observed core is about 100 m; eastern cores and isopycnal layers differ. No single depth is imposed on the route; surface SEC/NECC and deeper equatorial currents remain separate.
time_convention: Editorial geographic reach using Hormann and Brandt (2007) observations/model comparison and Napolitano et al. (2022) eastern-island study. Composite periods differ; no single dated or annual mean axis or seasonal geometry series.
source_locator: Introduction pp. 1–2: eastward equatorial flow, eastern bifurcation/termination-site context between 5 E and continental margin, Sao Tome around 6.6 E; sections 2–3 distinguish observations and model experiments.
source_citation: Napolitano, Alory, Dadou, Morel, Jouanno and Morvan (2022), Influence of the Gulf of Guinea Islands on the Atlantic Equatorial Undercurrent Circulation, JGR Oceans 127, e2021JC017999, doi:10.1029/2021JC017999.
source_license: Source article states Creative Commons Attribution license. Attributed regional facts paraphrased; no source figure or model/ADCP field copied.
coordinate_selection: OSW connects a published 35 W equatorial current section with a declared pre-island gate at 5 E, before the modeled/observed island interaction context near 6 E. Rounded equatorial waypoints and off-equatorial bends are editor-selected. The gates truncate known source/branch pathways and do not assert the current begins at 35 W or terminates at 5 E. No velocity curve, mooring line or model particle trajectory digitized.

alternative_routes.interpretation: OSW northward bend and shorter pre-island extent; not a seasonal observed axis or current width.
OSW southward bend and longer pre-island extent; no island branching or downstream return reconstructed.

scenario_rule: Three declared reach shapes crossed with uniform longitude offsets -0.25/0/+0.25 degrees and independent endpoint-latitude offsets -0.25/0/+0.25 degrees: 81 editorial cases, not width bounds, seasonal extremes or confidence limits.
remaining_gates: Review 35 W and pre-island truncation; source retroflections and eastern branches are not represented.
Obtain compatible depth/time-resolved velocity axis before physical length or seasonal dimensions.
Resolve island interaction and return-flow topology without treating generated eddies as named identities.
No occupied footprint, route-buffer width or whole-basin system length inferred.

supporting_sources.citation: Hormann and Brandt (2007), Atlantic Equatorial Undercurrent and associated cold tongue variability, JGR Oceans, doi:10.1029/2006JC003931.
supporting_sources.locator: Section 2.3.1.1 paragraph 14: observed 35 W current centered at equator with approximately 100 m core; paragraphs 16–18 distinguish 23 W and subsurface currents.
supporting_sources.role: Western observational section gate and layer/context distinction; no transport-to-length or depth-uniform inference.

method: Sum shortest WGS84 geodesic distances between successive OSW editorial vertices; no velocity field or current core is reconstructed.
map_land_check: All 81 routes, geodesically densified at spacing no greater than 10 km, avoid the coarse OSW atlas land mask in display coordinates. This is not a shelf-break, reef, bathymetric or high-resolution land-clearance verification.
state_relation_role: Editorial line/display-region crossing; physical current passage unresolved.
